objet: Documents needed to open the file
disponibilite: I remain available to answer any question on the above.

corps.p: Thank you for confirming both mandates. Here is what I need in order to open the file properly.
The agreement is drafted, in French and in English in the same document, and covers both the Swiss and the French matters. Two things are missing before I can send it to you for signature.

corps.b: a copy of your passport or identity card, together with a document evidencing your address dated within the last three months

corps.p: The second is a professional obligation on us before any new engagement, not a formality of our own making.

corps.b: the signed Transaction of 12 February 2025 in full, together with every earlier draft. Please also tell me who signed it, in what capacity and on what date. Your father died on 2 July 2024, before the first draft was circulated, so he cannot have signed it himself. This point governs the whole Swiss side and I do not want to write to the executor before it is settled.
the originals of the cantonal documents and of the two inventories, rather than the scans
the name of the executor, and of the Swiss lawyer who acted on the file
the emails you mention confirming that French inheritance tax was paid out of your father's estate, and any declaration or assessment notice you hold
your father's death certificate, and the document establishing that you are his sole heir
where your father was habitually resident at the date of his death. This determines the applicable law and the certificate I will need in order to act in France
whatever you know of the Neuilly apartment, however partial. Its address, and the name of any notary or lawyer who mentioned it to you

corps.p: Please send originals wherever you have them. Two of the nine points in your memorandum are not anomalies at all, but errors introduced when the documents were digitised. I would rather not build on a misread figure.
Several of these points would be quicker to cover in the conversation you suggested. I will come back to you separately on that.
